competencies.text: Explain plant organ interaction for material transport.

days.title: Plant Organs Working Together
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe the main plant organs and explain how they work together to transport water, minerals, and food throughout the plant.

🌿 The Plant as a System

Like animals, plants are made of organ systems that work together. In plants, the main organs are:

OrganMain FunctionStructure Support
RootsAbsorb water and minerals; anchor the plantRoot hairs increase surface area; branching reaches more soil
StemSupport and transport between roots and leavesContains vascular bundles (xylem + phloem); tall, strong
LeavesPhotosynthesis — make food (glucose) using sunlightBroad, flat, thin for maximum light absorption; contain stomata for gas exchange
FlowersReproduction — produce seedsBright colors and nectar attract pollinators
FruitsProtect seeds and aid dispersalFleshy or dry; may be eaten by animals

💧 The Vascular System — Plant

Plants have two types of transport tissues running through roots, stems, and leaves:

TissueWhat It TransportsDirectionDriving Force
XylemWater + dissolved mineralsUpward (roots → leaves)Transpiration pull + root pressure
PhloemFood (sugars/glucose)Both directions (source → sink)Pressure flow from high to low concentration

🌊 Water Transport — Step by Step

  1. Absorption: Root hairs absorb water and minerals from the soil by osmosis.
  2. Root pressure: Water moves into the xylem.
  3. Capillary action: Water molecules stick to xylem walls and each other, helping them move up.
  4. Transpiration pull: As water evaporates from leaves (through stomata), it pulls more water upward — like sucking through a straw.
  5. Delivery: Water reaches leaves, where it's used in photosynthesis and cools the plant.

🍯 Food Transport — Step by Step

  1. Production: Leaves produce glucose through photosynthesis.
  2. Loading: Glucose is converted to sucrose and loaded into phloem.
  3. Transport: Sucrose moves through phloem to where it's needed — growing tips, roots, fruits, storage organs.
  4. Unloading: Cells use the sugar for energy or store it as starch.

💨 Transpiration — The Plant's Cooling System

Transpiration is the loss of water vapor through stomata in the leaves.

  • Driven by sunlight, temperature, humidity, and wind.
  • Cools the plant (like sweating in humans).
  • Pulls water upward from roots to leaves.
  • Rate is higher on hot, dry, windy days.

Stomata are tiny openings on the underside of leaves that open and close to control gas exchange and water loss. Guard cells regulate them.

🌾 Real-Life Applications

  • Watering plants: Water the soil, not the leaves — roots are the entry point.
  • Wilting: When water loss (transpiration) exceeds uptake, plants droop. Water them quickly.
  • Girdling: Removing the bark (which contains phloem) kills a tree — food can't reach the roots.
  • Fertilizers: Provide minerals to the soil so roots can absorb them.
  • Pruning: Reduces leaf area, lowering transpiration and helping transplants survive.

🔬 The Big Idea

Plant organs form an integrated system — water, minerals, and food are transported through xylem and phloem; leaves produce food; roots anchor and absorb; stems support and connect everything. Remove one organ, and the whole system suffers.

📌 Quick Check

  • Which tissue transports water in plants? (Answer: xylem)
  • Which tissue transports food (sugars)? (Answer: phloem)
  • What is transpiration? (Answer: loss of water vapor from leaves through stomata)

days.title: Match Game — Plant Tissues
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each plant organ or tissue to its correct function. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Absorb water and minerals; anchor the plant
Supports the plant and transports materials between roots and leaves
Transports water and minerals upward from roots to leaves
Transports sugars from leaves to the rest of the plant
Loss of water vapor through stomata — pulls water up the plant
Tiny openings on the underside of leaves for gas exchange

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Transport in Plants
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌿 A farmer removes a complete ring of bark from around a tree trunk. A few months later, the tree dies. Why?

choices.label: A) The bark ring cut the phloem, so sugars from the leaves could no longer reach the roots — the roots starved
B) The tree lost its support
C) The tree became too cold
D) The bark was protecting against insects only

scenario.text: 🥀 A potted plant is left in the sun without water for two days. Its leaves droop and become soft. What has happened?

choices.label: A) Transpiration exceeded water uptake, so cells lost water and lost turgor pressure
B) The plant stopped making chlorophyll
C) The roots grew too long

scenario.text: 🌳 A gardener plants a small tree in soil with plenty of water but no minerals. It grows slowly and leaves yellow. Why?

choices.label: A) Plants need minerals (like nitrogen and magnesium) absorbed by roots to make chlorophyll and proteins
B) The plant has too much water
C) The tree is too young
D) Water alone is all plants need

scenario.text: ☀️ On a hot, windy day, a plant's transpiration rate is very high. What is likely to happen?

choices.label: A) The plant pulls up water faster from the roots to replace what's lost
B) The plant stops photosynthesis entirely
C) The plant starts to grow faster
D) Nothing changes — plants don't respond to weather

scenario.text: 🍯 Which plant tissue transports glucose from the leaves to the roots for storage?

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Botany Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Botany Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: Which plant organ is primarily responsible for absorbing water and minerals?
Which vascular tissue transports water upward from the roots?
Which vascular tissue transports sugar (food) throughout the plant?

choices.label: A) Loss of water vapor from leaves through stomata
B) Movement of food through phloem
C) Absorption of minerals by the roots
D) Production of glucose in leaves

escape.text: Why does removing a complete ring of bark kill a tree?

choices.label: A) It cuts the phloem, so sugars cannot reach the roots, which then starve and die
B) It removes the tree's protective armor
